l: The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus
s: the Lord hates sinner
q: For the Most High also hates sinners, and will repay vengeance to the ungodly.

l: The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus
s: enemy speaks sweetly (while planning in his heart to throw you into a pit)
q: The enemy will speak sweetly with his lips, and in his heart plan to throw you into a pit.

l: The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus
s: enemy seeks blood (when he finds opportunity)
q: The enemy may weep with his eyes, but if he finds opportunity, he will want more blood.

l: The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus
s: enemy pretends to help (while tripping you in adversity)
q: Pretending to help you, he will trip you.

l: The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus
s: distrust of the enemy is advised toward enemy (even when he humbles himself)
q: Though he humbles himself and walks bowed down, still be careful and beware of him.

l: The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus
s: distrust of the enemy forbids enemy (seating him next to you or on your right hand)
q: Don’t set him next to you, lest he overthrow you and stand in your place. Don’t let him sit on your right hand, lest he seek to take your seat

l: The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus
s: sinner stays with associate a while (leaves if you falter)
q: For a while he will stay with you, and if you falter, he will not stay.

l: The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus
s: the Lord repays vengeance to sinner (the ungodly)
q: For the Most High also hates sinners, and will repay vengeance to the ungodly.

l: The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus
s: the Lord rewards godly man (if the man himself does not)
q: Do good to a godly man, and you will find a reward— if not from him, then from the Most High.

l: The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus
s: godly man is recipient of almsgiving (should be given to)
q: Give to the godly man, and don’t help the sinner.

l: The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus
s: sinner is not recipient of almsgiving (should not be helped)
q: Give to the godly man, and don’t help the sinner.

l: The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus
s: almsgiving brings reward (when done for a godly man)
q: Do good to a godly man, and you will find a reward— if not from him, then from the Most High.

l: The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus
s: enemy has wickedness like corrosion in copper
q: Never trust your enemy, for his wickedness is like corrosion in copper.

l: The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus
s: enemy is hidden in adversity (not hidden in adversity)
q: His enemy won’t be hidden in adversity.

l: The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus
s: enemy feels toward prosperity grief (in a man's prosperity)
q: In a man’s prosperity, his enemies are grieved.

l: The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus
s: fellowship with the powerful advised distance neither pressing nor standing far off
q: Don’t press him, lest you be thrust back. Don’t stand far off, lest you be forgotten.

l: The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus
s: poor man is prey of rich man (likened to wild donkeys and lions)
q: likewise poor men are feeding grounds for the rich.

l: The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus
s: poor man is regarded as abomination (by the rich)
q: a poor man is an abomination to the rich.

l: The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus
s: rich man receives from friends support when shaken
q: When a rich man is shaken, he is supported by his friends

l: The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus
s: poor man receives from friends rejection when down (humble man)
q: when the humble is down, he is pushed away even by his friends.

l: The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus
s: rich man receives from others many helpers and justification when he falls
q: When a rich man falls, there are many helpers. He speaks things not to be spoken, and men justify him.

l: The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus
s: poor man receives from others rebuke and being ignored (humble man who falls)
q: A humble man falls, and men rebuke him. He utters wisdom, and is not listened to.

l: The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus
s: rich man is listened to all keep silence and extol him
q: A rich man speaks, and all keep silence. They extol what he says to the clouds.

l: The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus
s: poor man is dismissed when speaking Who is this? (stumbling leads to being overthrown)
q: A poor man speaks, and they say, “Who is this?” If he stumbles, they will help to overthrow him.

l: The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus
s: fellowship with the powerful is discouraged with rich man (one mightier and richer than yourself)
q: Have no fellowship with one who is mightier and richer than yourself.

l: The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus
s: earthen pot and kettle illustrates fellowship with the powerful (the kettle strikes and the pot is dashed in pieces)
q: What fellowship would the earthen pot have with the kettle? The kettle will strike, and the pot will be dashed in pieces.

l: The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus
s: rich man behavior when wrong threatens (after doing wrong)
q: The rich man does a wrong and threatens.

l: The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus
s: poor man behavior when wronged apologizes
q: The poor is wronged and apologizes.

l: The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus
s: rich man treats associates exploits when profitable, forsakes when in need (toward those who associate with him)
q: If you are profitable, he will exploit you. If you are in need, he will forsake you.

l: The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus
s: rich man deals deceptively with those he needs (smiles and gives false hope)
q: Does he need you? Then he will deceive you, smile at you, and give you hope.

l: The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus
s: fellowship with the powerful advised manner reserved (when a mighty man invites you)
q: If a mighty man invites you, be reserved, and he will invite you more.

l: The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus
s: miser is a evil person
q: A miser is evil.

l: The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus
s: Wisdom has attribute glory
q: By her he will be covered from heat, and will lodge in her glory.

l: The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus
s: man who meditates on wisdom is blessed
q: Blessed is the man who meditates on wisdom, and who reasons by his understanding.

l: The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus
s: man who meditates on wisdom will have knowledge of Wisdom (her secrets)
q: He who considers her ways in his heart will also have knowledge of her secrets.

l: The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus
s: man who meditates on wisdom will lodge near Wisdom (pitches tent near her)
q: He will pitch his tent near at hand to her, and will lodge in a lodging where good things are.

l: The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus
s: my son is advised to treat himself well (according to what he has)
q: My son, according to what you have, treat yourself well, and bring worthy offerings to the Lord.

l: The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus
s: my son is advised to bring offerings (worthy offerings to the Lord)
q: My son, according to what you have, treat yourself well, and bring worthy offerings to the Lord.

l: The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus
s: death is inevitable (will not wait)
q: Remember that death will not wait, and that the covenant of Hades hasn’t been shown to you.

l: The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus
s: death is decreed for all flesh (covenant from the beginning)
q: All flesh grows old like a garment, for the covenant from the beginning is, “You must die!”

l: The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus
s: miser disregards souls (turns away)
q: He turns away and disregards souls.

l: The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus
s: miser is unsuited to riches
q: Riches are not appropriate for a stingy person.

l: The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus
s: miser gathers goods for others (by denying himself)
q: He who gathers by denying himself gathers for others. Others will revel in his goods.

l: The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus
s: miser begrudges bread (bread is lacking at his table)
q: A miser begrudges bread, and it is lacking at his table.

l: The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus
s: miser has trait covetousness (eye not satisfied with his portion)
q: A covetous man’s eye is not satisfied with his portion.

l: The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus
s: Wisdom has part secrets
q: He who considers her ways in his heart will also have knowledge of her secrets.

l: The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus
s: Wisdom has part house (with windows, doors and walls)
q: He who lodges close to her house will also fasten a nail in her walls.

l: The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus
s: Wisdom provides shelter (covers from heat; has branches)
q: He will set his children under her shelter, and will rest under her branches.

l: The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus
s: those who love the Lord obtains Wisdom
q: He who fears the Lord will do this. He who has possession of the law will obtain her.

l: The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus
s: the Lord hates abomination (every abomination)
q: The Lord hates every abomination; and those who fear him don’t love them.

l: The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus
s: the Lord made man (from the beginning)
q: He himself made man from the beginning and left him in the hand of his own counsel.

l: The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus
s: man has free choice (left in the hand of his own counsel)
q: He himself made man from the beginning and left him in the hand of his own counsel.

l: The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus
s: free choice enables keeping the commandments (faithfulness is a matter of choice)
q: If you choose, you can keep the commandments. To be faithful is a matter of your choice.

l: The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus
s: man has before him life and death (receives whichever he likes)
q: Before man is life and death. Whichever he likes, it will be given to him.

l: The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus
s: the Lord has attribute mighty in power (sees all things)
q: He is mighty in power, and sees all things.

l: The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus
s: the Lord watches those who love the Lord (his eyes are upon them)
q: His eyes are upon those who fear him.

l: The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus
s: the Lord knows man (every act of man)
q: He knows every act of man.

l: The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus
s: the Lord commands no man to be ungodly (gives no license to sin)
q: He has not commanded any man to be ungodly. He has not given any man license to sin.

l: The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus
s: Wisdom meets like mother (toward he who fears the Lord)
q: She will meet him like a mother, and receive him like a wife married in her virginity.

l: The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus
s: Wisdom feeds bread of understanding (to he who fears the Lord)
q: She will feed him with bread of understanding and give him water of wisdom to drink.

l: The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus
s: Wisdom exalts those who love the Lord (above his neighbors)
q: She will exalt him above his neighbors.

l: The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus
s: those who love the Lord relies on Wisdom (will not be moved)
q: He will rely upon her, and will not be confounded.

l: The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus
s: those who love the Lord inherits everlasting name (also joy and a crown of gladness)
q: He will inherit joy, a crown of gladness, and an everlasting name.

l: The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus
s: Wisdom is far from pride
q: She is far from pride.

l: The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus
s: foolish men obtains Wisdom (negated: will not obtain her)
q: Foolish men will not obtain her.

l: The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus
s: sinners sees Wisdom (negated: will not see her)
q: Sinners will not see her.

l: The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus
s: the Lord is not pacified toward giants of old time (they revolted in their strength)
q: He was not pacified toward the giants of old time, who revolted in their strength.

l: The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus
s: sinners gather in congregation (a fire is kindled in it)
q: In a congregation of sinners, a fire will be kindled.

l: The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus
s: sinners does not escape plunder (will not escape with it)
q: The sinner will not escape with plunder.

l: The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus
s: creation is boundless
q: what is my soul in a boundless creation?

l: The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus
s: works of the Lord are mostly hidden (like an unseen tempest)
q: Like a tempest which no man can see, so, the majority of his works are hidden.

l: The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus
s: works of the Lord are arranged for all time (by the Lord)
q: He arranged his works for all time, and their beginnings to their generations.

l: The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus
s: works of the Lord do not hunger or weary (never cease from their works)
q: They aren’t hungry or weary, and they don’t cease from their works.

l: The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus
s: the Lord does not spare Lot's neighbors (abhorred for their pride)
q: He didn’t spare Lot’s neighbors, whom he abhorred for their pride.

l: The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus
s: works of the Lord never disobey his word
q: They will never disobey his word.

l: The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus
s: divine mercy and wrath is proportioned great (his correction is as great as his mercy)
q: As his mercy is great, so is his correction also.

l: The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus
s: divine judgment has boundaries set his works (determined from their making)
q: In the judgment of the Lord are his works from the beginning. From the making of them he determined their boundaries.

l: The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus
s: the Lord does not pity people of perdition (taken away in their sins)
q: He didn’t pity the people of perdition who were taken away in their sins,

l: The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus
s: the Lord is mighty to forgive
q: mercy and wrath are both with him who is mighty to forgive, and he pours out wrath.

l: The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus
s: the Lord judges man according to his works
q: He judges a man according to his works.

l: The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus
s: the Lord fills earth with blessings (after looking at the earth)
q: After this also the Lord looked at the earth and filled it with his blessings.

l: The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus
s: the Lord has covenant (described as afar off)
q: For his covenant is afar off.

l: The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus
s: ungodly children is worse than dying childless
q: to die childless than to have ungodly children.

l: The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus
s: ungodly children is a unprofitable (should not be desired)
q: Don’t desire a multitude of unprofitable children, neither delight in ungodly sons.

l: The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus
s: the Lord creates mankind (out of earth)
q: The Lord created mankind out of earth, and turned them back to it again.

l: The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus
s: the Lord gives law of life (to mankind as heritage)
q: He added to them knowledge, and gave them a law of life for a heritage.

l: The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus
s: the Lord makes covenant (with mankind, everlasting)
q: He made an everlasting covenant with them, and showed them his decrees.

l: The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus
s: the Lord commands mankind (to beware of all unrighteousness, each man concerning his neighbor)
q: He said to them, “Beware of all unrighteousness.” So he gave them commandment, each man concerning his neighbor.

l: The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus
s: the Lord sees mankind (their ways are ever before him and not hidden)
q: Their ways are ever before him. They will not be hidden from his eyes.

l: The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus
s: the Lord appoints ruler for nation (every nation)
q: For every nation he appointed a ruler, but Israel is the Lord’s portion.

l: The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus
s: Israel is portion of the Lord
q: For every nation he appointed a ruler, but Israel is the Lord’s portion.

l: The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus
s: sins and unrighteousness is known to the Lord (not hidden, all before him)
q: Their iniquities are not hidden from him. All their sins are before the Lord.

l: The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus
s: the Lord regards as precious alms and kindness of a man (as a signet and pupil of the eye)
q: With him the alms of a man is as a signet. He will keep a man’s kindness as the pupil of the eye.

l: The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus
s: the Lord repays mankind (upon their head)
q: Afterwards he will rise up and repay them, and give their repayment upon their head.

l: The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus
s: repentance and mercy is granted by the Lord (a return to those who repent)
q: However to those who repent he grants a return. He comforts those who are losing hope.

l: The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus
s: mankind is made from earth
q: The Lord created mankind out of earth, and turned them back to it again.

l: The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus
s: the Lord comforts those losing hope
q: However to those who repent he grants a return. He comforts those who are losing hope.

l: The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus
s: repentance and mercy is characterized by great mercy and forgiveness (of the Lord to those who turn to him)
q: How great is the mercy of the Lord, and his forgiveness to those who turn to him!

l: The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus
s: mankind is not immortal (not capable of everything)
q: For humans are not capable of everything, because the son of man is not immortal.

l: The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus
s: mankind is made of earth and ashes
q: while all men are earth and ashes.

l: The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus
s: mankind has lifespan days by number (set time)
q: He gave them days by number, and a set time, and gave them authority over the things that are on it.

l: The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus
s: mankind has authority over things on earth (given by the Lord)
q: He gave them days by number, and a set time, and gave them authority over the things that are on it.

l: The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus
s: mankind is made according to image of the Lord
q: He endowed them with strength proper to them, and made them according to his own image.

l: The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus
s: mankind has dominion over beasts and birds (fear of man put upon all flesh)
q: He put the fear of man upon all flesh, and gave him dominion over beasts and birds.

l: The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus
s: mankind has faculty understanding (counsel, tongue, eyes, ears, heart)
q: He gave them counsel, tongue, eyes, ears, and heart to have understanding.

l: The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus
s: mankind possesses knowledge of wisdom (knows good and evil)
q: He filled them with the knowledge of wisdom, and showed them good and evil.

l: The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus
s: mankind has inheritance law of life (heritage)
q: He added to them knowledge, and gave them a law of life for a heritage.

l: The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus
s: the Lord creates universe (he who lives forever)
q: He who lives forever created the whole universe.

l: The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus
s: word and gift has ranking word is better than a gift
q: So a word is better than a gift.

l: The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus
s: word and gift are found with gracious person (both together)
q: Both are with a gracious person.

l: The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus
s: self-restraint and desires advises restrain appetites (do not follow lusts)
q: Don’t go after your lusts. Restrain your appetites.
